다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

Sociologists classify generations based on an
individual’s birth year. The four most recent generations
are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or
millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are
named so because the birth rate was significantly
higher when they were born. But since Korea and
the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases
during different periods, their classifications of baby
boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers
are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in
Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955
and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its
name from the title of a book written by Douglas
Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in
their twenties in that era had a relaxed and
laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born
after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996)
and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are
also called millennials because they became adults
with the beginning of the new millennium.
choices: How Are Generations Classified and Named?
Why Do Generational Values Change Over Time?
Why Are Generational Labels Socially Significant?
How Do Life Stages Shape Generational Identity?
How Are Generations Interpreted in ContemporarySociety?

B: Hello, everyone. I’m Mahir. Today I’d like to tell
you about a three-day space program called
Experience Space. I took part in this program
because I’ve always been curious about living in
space. Let me tell you a little bit about what I
did in the program. On the first day, I learned
how to put on a spacesuit. It was awkward and
uncomfortable to wear at first, but with the help
of the trainers I got used to walking around in
it. On the second day, I learned how to move
around in zero gravity. I felt dizzy, but it was
actually fun to float around. On the last day, I
tried eating space food, which was very different
from what I usually eat. The food didn’t taste
good, but it was an interesting experience. All in
all, the program was very exciting. I wish I could
travel to space on a spaceship one day.

The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a
generation are closely related. ⓐBroadly speaking,
each generation is defined by the birth years of its
members. According to the theory of generational
cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular
generation are socialized in distinct conditions
compared to other generations. They experience
similar political, economic, and social events during
their early stages of life, ⓑwhich shape their beliefs,
values, and behaviors in similar ways.
The
cohort
effect
results
in
characteristic
differences
between
generations.
For
instance,
Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis,
ⓒalso known as the International Monetary Fund
(IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time,
and thus experienced great employment instability.
ⓓThis may have led them to prioritize secure
employment for their children. In contrast, Gen Zers
grew up with smartphones, and this earned them
the “digital natives” label. ⓔThey are accustomed to
getting their news, information, and advice from
social media. Their strength in using digital media,
however, often leads them to lack social skills.

In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, which was 380,000 km
away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil Armstrong
became the first person to walk on the Moon,
famously declaring, “That’s one small step for a
man, one giant leap for mankind.” The most recent
Moon landing took place in 1972, and a total of 12
astronauts have walked on the Moon. More than 50
years later, NASA declared its plan to go back to
the Moon and began the Artemis Project. Named
after Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis, the project aims
to use innovative technologies to land the first
woman and the first person of color on the Moon
in the near future. After exploring the Moon, NASA
is planning to take the next giant leap: sending the
first astronauts to Mars.

young. Remember how we used to look for the
best place for patbingsu?

choices: I can relate to you.

M: In today’s lecture, I’m going to talk about two
different ways to ask for permission in English:
“Can I ... ?” versus “Do you mind if I ... ?”
Depending on the context, you may want to
use one or the other. For example, let’s say you
want to ask your close friend if you can borrow
a pen. In this situation, you might say, “Can I
borrow your pen?” It may sound strange to say,
“Do you mind if I borrow your pen?” On the
other hand, imagine you want to sit on a bench
in a park, but someone is already sitting there.
In this situation, it’d be more appropriate to
say, “Do you mind if I sit next to you?” than
“Can I sit next to you?” This is because you’d
generally want to be more polite when you’re
talking to people you don’t know. You should
use polite or casual styles of communication
depending on who you are talking to and how
close you are to them. So, choose expressions
carefully when communicating with others.
choices: Asking for permission in English is difficult, soyou should avoid it whenever possible.
You should always use casual expressions whentalking to friends or people you know well.
Politeness in English depends only on the wordsyou choose, not on the situation or the person.
English has many ways to ask questions, and itis important to know the difference betweenthem.
When asking for permission in English, it iscrucial to choose the expression based on thesituation and the person.
solution: 영어로 허락을 요청하는 표현으로 좀 더 격의 없는 방식인 “Can I …?”와 좀 더 공손함을 나타내는 표현인 “Do you mind if I …?”가 있으며, 이 두 가지 의사소통 방식은 상대가 가까운 친구인지 공원에서 만난 모르는 사람인지에 따라 적절히 구분 해서 써야 한다는 예시를 소개하고, 다른 사람들과의 의사소통 에서 신중하게 표현을 선택하는 것이 중요하다고 결론짓고 있 으므로, 글의 요지로 ❺ ‘영어로 허락을 요청할 때, 상황과 상 대에 근거하여 표현을 선택하는 것이 중요하다.’가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 2과

light pollution from satellites.

body:
In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, (A)[where / which] was
380,000 km away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil
Armstrong became the first person (B)[walked / to
walk] on the Moon, famously declaring, “That’s one
small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.”
The most recent Moon landing took place in 1972,
and a total of 12 astronauts have walked on the
Moon. More than 50 years later, NASA declared its
plan to go back to the Moon and began the
Artemis Project. (C)[Named / Naming] after Apollo’s
twin sister, Artemis, the project aims to use
innovative technologies to land the first woman and
the first person of color on the Moon in the near
future. After exploring the Moon, NASA is planning
to take the next giant leap: sending the first
astronauts to Mars.

solution: (A) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 동사 was의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was 380,000 km away)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 주격관계대명사 which가 적절하다. (B) 동사(became)가 있는 완전한 절(Neil Armstrong became the first person)에 이어지는 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ‘걸은 (최초의 사람)’이라는 뜻으로 명사구 the first person을 수식해 야 하므로 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to walk가 적절하다. (C) 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰여 주절 주어 the project를 부 연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리로, the project가 ‘이름이 붙여진’ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘name ~ after … (~을 …의 이름을 따서 짓다)’의 전치사 after와 명사구 Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis가 이어지므로, ‘~ be named after …(~가 …의 이름을 따서 지어지다)’의 과거분사 Named가 적절하다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓐ have caused → has caused (명사구 The increasing number of satellites를 과거분사구 launched into orbit이 수식해 주어부를 이루고 있으며, 이어지 는 동사 자리에 과거부터 지금까지 ‘야기해 왔다’라는 의미로 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 주어의 핵심 인 number가 단수명사이므로 단수 조동사 has로 수일치 시켜 야 한다. 따라서 have caused를 has caused로 고친다.) ⓒ have launched → have been launched (주어 Enormous numbers of low-flying satellites가 복수명사 구이고, 글의 흐름상 과거부터 현재까지 ‘발사되어 온’ 것이므 로 복수 조동사(have)로 수일치한 현재완료가 쓰이는 것은 적 절하나, 주어가 ‘발사되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로, 현재완료 능동태인 have launched를 현재완료 수동태 (have[has]+been+p.p.)인 have been launched로 고친다.) ⓔ remain → remains (주어 Approximately 37 percent of the global population에 이어지는 동사 자리에 ‘계속 ~인 상태이다’라는 뜻으로 뒤의 형용사 unconnected를 보어로 취하는 불완전자동사 remain이 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, ‘숫자+percent of+명사(구)’가 주어일 때 이어지는 동사의 수는 of 뒤의 명사(구)에 수일치 시키므로, 단 수명사구 the global population에 수일치한 단수동사를 써야 한다. 따라서 복수동사 remain을 단수동사 remains로 고친다.) ⓖ we can ensure → can we ensure (Only를 포함한 부사구가 강조를 위해 문두에 쓰였으므로 이어 지는 절의 주어와 동사를 도치시켜야 하며, 조동사가 있는 경 우 ‘부사구+조동사+주어+동사원형 ~’의 어순이 되므로 we can ensure을 can we ensure로 고친다.)

body:
(A)흔히 현대 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지로 여겨지는 Alan
Turing은 컴퓨터 메모리의 개념을 개발하고 최초로 전
자 저장 프로그램을 만든 것으로 유명했다. In 1950,
in his research paper titled “Computing Machinery
and Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking
question: Can machines think? This research paper
was the first to provide a framework for thinking
about machine intelligence. Turing wanted to see if
a machine could be as intelligent as humans and
asked himself, “If a machine could imitate human
behavior, why wouldn’t it be able to think like a
human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”
1950: Alan Turing introduced the Turing test.
1956: The term “artificial intelligence” was coined.

choices: Turing introduced the Turing test as a practicalexperiment to improve computer performance.
Turingarguedthatmachinescouldthinkindependently of human behavior and interaction.
Turing attempted to define human intelligenceby comparing it with the operational mechanismsof machines.
Turing emphasized the technical limitations ofearly computers and questioned their ability toreplicate human intelligence.
Turing devised the Turing Test to see ifmachines could think like humans and predictedthe possibility that such machines could becreated.

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the first
to provide a framework for thinking about machine
intelligence. Turing wanted to see if a machine could
be as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that __________
__________________________________________________________.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the computer could store and retrieve informationefficiently
the computer might surpass human emotionalunderstanding
the computer followed logical rules designed byhumans
the computer could perform tasks faster thanhumans
the computer had the ability to think like a human
solution: ‘기계가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있는가’라는 질문은 Turing이 ‘모 방 게임’을 고안하게 만들었으며, 튜링 테스트로도 알려진 이 게임에서 참가자가 컴퓨터와 인간의 답변을 구별하지 못했다 면, 그 컴퓨터는 튜링 테스트를 통과한 것이 되었다는 내용 뒤 에 이어지므로, 이러한 결과로부터 기계가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있다는 것이 추론되었을지도 모른다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따 라서 빈칸에는 ❺ ‘컴퓨터가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있는 능력을 가졌다’가 알맞다.

body:
In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, which was 380,000 km
away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil Armstrong
became the first person to walk on the Moon,
famously declaring, “That’s one small step for a
man, one giant leap for mankind.” The most recent
Moon landing took place in 1972, and a total of 12
astronauts have walked on the Moon. More than 50
years later, NASA declared its plan to go back to
the Moon and began the Artemis Project. Named
after Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis, the project aims
to use innovative technologies to land the first
woman and the first person of color on the Moon
in the near future. After exploring the Moon, NASA
is planning to take the next giant leap: sending the
first astronauts to Mars.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the historical influence of Greek mythology onmodern scientific research fields
the influence of NASA’s lunar exploration programson public interest in science and technology
the similarities and differences between theApollo and Artemis projects for lunar exploration
theevolutionofNASA’slunarexplorationprograms whose names were inspired by themythological figures
the challenges faced by NASA’s lunar explorationprogramsandthesolutionsdevelopedtoovercome them
solution: NASA가 그리스 신화에 나오는 태양의 신 아폴로에게서 영감 을 받아 최초의 달 프로젝트를 아폴로 프로그램이라고 이름 지었고, 1969년에 닐 암스트롱이 최초로 달에 발을 디딘 후 1972년에는 12명의 우주 비행사가 달을 밟았으며, 그로부터 50년 후 시작된 아르테미스 프로젝트는 아폴로의 쌍둥이 누나 인 아르테미스의 이름을 딴 것으로, 가까운 미래에 최초의 여 성이자 최초의 유색인종을 달에 착륙시키는 것을 목표로 하고 있다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ❹ ‘이름이 신화 의 인물들에서 영감을 받은 NASA의 달 탐사 프로그램들의 발 전’이 알맞다.

day.(나는 언 젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험할 수 있으면 좋겠어.)’라고 말하며 자신의 개인적 바람을 나타내고 있으므로, 어떤 일이 이루어질 가능성에 대해 의구심을 나타내는 표현인 ② ‘내가 언젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험을 할 수 있을지 의심스러워 보여.’로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 오답 ① 내가 언젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험할 기회를 가질 수 있다면 좋을 텐데. 관계사절을 연결한다. <보기> 의 one of 뒤에 관계대명사 which를 쓰고, one에 수일치 한 단수동사 is와 보어인 명사구 space debris를 쓴다. 16) ⑤: 위성으로 인한 빛 공해 때문에 밤하늘의 밝기가 계속 증가하여 2030년에는 자연적인 어둠보다 최대 12% 더 밝아질 것이라고 설명하므로, 이러한 빛 공해의 결과로 야기되는 문제가 구조하는 데 도움이 된다. 18) ④: NASA가 그리스 신화에 나오는 태양의 신 아폴로에게 서 영감을 받아 최초의 달 프로젝트를 아폴로 프로그 램이라고 이름 지었고, 1969년에 닐 암스트롱이 최초 로 달에 발을 디딘 후 1972년에는 12명의 우주 비행사 가 달을 밟았으며, 그로부터 50년 후 시작된 아르테미 스 프로젝트는 아폴로의 쌍둥이 누나인 과학과 기술에 대한 대중의 관심에 미친 영향 ③ 달 탐사를 위한 아폴로와 아르테미스 프로젝트 사 이의 유사점과 차이점 ⑤ NASA의 달 탐사 프로그램들이 직면했던 도전들과 그것들을 극복하기 위해 개발된 해결책들 19) (1) Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon (2) to use innovative technologies to land the first woman and the first person of color on the Moon 질문 (1) 1969년에 아폴로 프로그램을 통해 어떤 역사적인 성취 가 이루어졌는가? → 1969년에, 닐 암스트롱은 달 위를 걸은 최초의 사람이 되었다. (2) 아르테미스 프로젝트는 가까운 미래에 무엇을 달성하는 것을 목표로 하는가? → 그것은 혁신적인 기술을 사용하여 최초의 여성과 최초 의 유색인종을 달에 착륙시키는 것을 목표로 한다. 20) ③: (A) TV 신호, 라디오, 인터넷, 전화 서비스를 지원한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 이를 통해 위성 데이터가 전 세계 통신을 용이하게 한다는 흐름으로 facilitating(용이하게 하는 것)이 알맞다. delaying 지연시키는 것 (B) 위성은 날씨 예보를 위해 데이터를 수집한다는 것 에 이어, 지구 대기와 다른 행성, 별을 탐사하는 과학 연구와 실험에도 사용된다는 내용이 언급되므로, 위성 이 널리 사용된다는 흐름으로 extensively(광범위하게)가 알맞다. sparsely 드물게 (C) 고해상도 이미지는 군사 감시를 포함한 여러 용도 로 활용된다는 내용이 이어지므로, 위성 데이터가 관측 및 모니터링 목적에도 매우 유용하다는 흐름이 되는 invaluable(매우 귀중한)이 알맞다. valueless 쓸모없는

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and ⓐmaking the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his
research
paper
ⓑwas
titled
“Computing
Machinery
and
Intelligence,”
he
posed
a
thought-provoking question: Can machines think?
This research paper was the first to provide a
framework for thinking about machine intelligence.
Turing wanted to see ⓒwhich a machine could be
as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” ⓓwhat also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed ⓔdistinguishing
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.

deep
learning
artificial

The engineers didn’t instruct the neural network to

the images. They waited to find out if the neural

images and form classifications in an unsupervised
manner. After the neural network processed the

detect three images: a human face, a human body,
and
a
cat.

seemingly
simple
research
represented
a
significant
advancement
in
the
unsupervised image recognition tasks of neural

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the first
to provide a framework for thinking about machine
intelligence. Turing wanted to see if a machine could
be as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
__________________________________________________________.

Often ⓐconsider the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the
first ⓑto provide a framework for thinking about
machine intelligence. (A)Turing은 기계가 인간만큼 지
능적일 수 있는지 알아보기를 원했으며, ‘만약 기계가
인간 행동을 모방할 수 있다면, 왜 그것이 인간처럼
생각할 수 없겠는가?’라는 질문을 스스로에게 던졌다.
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked ⓒstating which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. ⓓIt might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted ⓔthat this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”
1950: Alan Turing introduced the Turing test.
1956: The term “artificial intelligence” was coined.

to analyze the psychological effects of human–computer interaction in early artificial intelligenceresearch
to evaluate the practical limitations of earlycomputer systems in mimicking human intelligence
to compare the Turing Test with other methodsfor measuring artificial intelligence
to argue that machines will eventually surpasshuman intelligence
solution: 현대 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지라고 불리는 Alan Turing이 1950년 자신의 연구 논문에서 “기계가 생각할 수 있는가?”라는 질문을 제기하며 기계 지능에 대해 생각하기 위한 틀을 최초로 제공 했고, 튜링 테스트를 고안함으로써 지능을 가진 기계가 만들어 질 가능성에 대해 예측하고 상상했다는 내용으로, 인공 지능이 만들어질 가능성을 제기하고 이론적 틀을 확립한 Alan Turing 의 업적에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 목적으로 ❶ ‘인공지 능을 만들 가능성을 제기하고 그 이론적인 기반을 확립한 Alan Turing을 업적을 설명하기 위해’가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 3과

(B) A network of 16,000 computer processors was

video
images
and
form
classifications
in
an
unsupervised manner. (E) This seemingly simple
research represented a significant advancement in
the unsupervised image recognition tasks of neural
networks and marked the beginning of a new era
of artificial intelligence research.
Many experts predict that artificial intelligence will
impact every aspect of 21st century life. AI will
improve the way ⓓhow we work, play, and
communicate. Along with hope and excitement,
there are also concerns. Some people argue that AI
will take our jobs and eventually control human

stroll around the charming, medieval town. Upon
arrival, the two towers of St. Kilian Cathedral
ⓑwelcome you. And within a five-minute walk of
the towers, the Würzburg Residence, a UNESCO
World Heritage Site, will be on full display with
Court Gardens and Residence Square. This beautiful
palace was built by the most ⓒprominent architects
and artists of the 18th century from Austria, France,
Italy, and Germany. But the ⓓbeauty of the city
doesn’t stop there. For a more ⓔadventurous
experience, take a stroll along the banks of the
Main and watch the sun set behind the skyline. It’s
an excellent photo spot, so I took some during the
sunset.

(C) 동사 hurried 뒤에 접속사 없이 다른 동사가 쓰일 수 없고 ‘서둘러 ~하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘hurry+to부정사’를 사용하므로, to arrange가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 1과

On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed
London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69
dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. (A)그들은 앞
으로의 여정이 역사상 가장 험난한 모험들 중 하나가
될 줄을 거의 알지 못했다.
The crew members were full of excitement, but
when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on
January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear.
“Oh, my! It’s frozen like an almond in the middle of
a chocolate bar!” cried one of the crew members.
Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship
and set up camp on the floating ice, where they
would be forced to spend the winter. Each man
was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one
of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping
bags to other crew members and chose to stay
with the group’s more troublesome characters who
could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats
were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet.
The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered
from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on
which they were camped began cracking beneath
them. Shackleton walked around inspecting the ice
regularly for the crew members’ safety. Some
nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their
tents, moving their camp to a more secure area
where the ice was less likely to break.

윗글의 두 번째 문단의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the Endurance’s escape from the thick pack iceunder Shackleton’s leadership
Shackleton and the Endurance crew who wereunprepared for the Antarctic expedition
how Shackleton and the Endurance crew avoidedall major dangers in the Antarctic
the anxiety and fear felt by the crew as theEndurance became trapped in thick pack ice
the Endurance stuck in thick pack ice andShackleton’s leadership during the struggle onthe ice
solution: 남극 대륙 횡단에 나선 Shackleton과 대원들이 1915년 1월 18 일 Endurance 호가 두꺼운 총빙(叢氷)에 갇히는 사건을 겪게 되어 Endurance 호를 버리고 Shackleton의 리더십 아래 대원 들이 얼음 위에서 혹독한 겨울을 나는 과정을 이야기했으므로, ❺ ‘두꺼운 총빙(叢氷)에 갇힌 Endurance 호와 얼음 위에서의 악전고투 중 Shackleton의 리더십’이 주제로 알맞다.

coining the term “a wounded healer.” He stated
that “We don’t get wounded alone, and we don’t
heal alone.” Then what does “a wounded healer”
mean? (A)상처 입은 치유자들은 그들의 고통스러운
경험이 그들로 하여금 다른 사람들을 도울 수 있게 하
는 사람들이다. They are good listeners and view all
experiences as opportunities to understand others’
hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to
become a healer. People who go through suffering
do not always become healers. It is those who
overcome suffering who can become wounded
healers,
and
they
can
evolve
into
“wounded
leaders.” The wounded leaders are those who

who have dealt with their wounds find themselves
more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is
characterized
by
the
ability
to
embrace
the
uncomfortable but necessary process of healing:
accepting different perspectives and focusing on
personal development while pursuing their goals.

On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton (A)[departed /
reached] London on the ship Endurance with 27
men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent.
Little did they know the journey ahead would be
one of the most challenging adventures in history.
The crew members were full of excitement, but
when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on
January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear.
“Oh, my! It’s (B)[drifting / frozen] like an almond in
the middle of a chocolate bar!” cried one of the
crew members. Shackleton and his men had to
abandon their ship and set up camp on the
floating ice, ⓐ[which / where] they would be forced
to spend the winter. Each man ⓑ[given / was
given] a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of
five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping
bags to other crew members and chose to stay
with the group’s more troublesome characters who
could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats
were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet.
The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered
from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on
which they were camped began (C)[cracking / freezing]
beneath them. Shackleton walked around inspecting
the ice regularly for the crew members’ safety. Some
nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their
tents, ⓒ[moving / moved] their camp to a more
secure area where the ice was less likely to break.

The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice
hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no

experiences enable them (A)__________________________.
They are good listeners and view all experiences as
opportunities
to
understand
others’
hardships.
Indeed, one should be wounded to become a
healer. People who go through suffering do not
always become healers. It is those who overcome
suffering who can become wounded healers, and
they can evolve into “wounded leaders.” The
wounded leaders are those who understand wounds
and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership
would be transformative because they lead to
deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and
greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt
with their wounds find themselves more at peace.
